data.cultural_impact: Krishnaa is a popular name among Hindus and holds significant cultural importance in Indian history and art. The name is often associated with the deity Lord Krishna, who is considered one of the avatars of the god Vishnu. Krishnaa is also the name of Radha, the beloved consort of Lord Krishna in devotional literature and art. Many Hindu families give the name Krishnaa to their female children, and it has a rich cultural significance in various Indian traditions.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, Krishnaa represents the divine and all-pervading consciousness. It is believed that Lord Krishna, as an incarnation of God, embodies love, compassion, and divine mischief. Krishnaa is also considered a manifestation of both the divine feminine and the divine masculine, as seen in the relationship between Lord Krishna and Radha. The name reflects the spiritual beauty of the divine presence, which is beyond form and traverses all aspects of the cosmos. It is a reminder of the eternal love and inner peace that we can access through the practice of devotion, selfless service, and spiritual growth.

historical_references.reference: Krishna (as described in Mahabharata) was an avatar of the god Vishnu who appeared in the Dwapara Yuga to establish Dharma, kill the demon King Kamsa, and ultimately defeat the wicked King Shishupala.
historical_references.context: Mahabharata, an Indian epic, describes Krishna's role in the great battle of Kurukshetra between the Pandava princes and their cousins, the Kauravas.

historical_references.reference: Another reference suggests Krishna was born approximately 3228 BCE in Mathura, and he was the eighth son of Devaki and Vasudeva. He was a central figure in the Mahabharata epic, as well as in the Bhagavad Gita, a 700-verse Hindu scripture.
historical_references.context: Bhagavad Gita is considered an essential text in Hinduism and is one of the most popular scriptures in the world.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Krishnaa' is deeply rooted in Hindu mythology and is synonymous with divine love and kindness. In modern times, Krishnaa is not only revered as a deity but is also a popular figure in various forms of popular culture. On social media platforms like Instagram, you can find numerous accounts dedicated to sharing images and stories of Lord Krishna. On YouTube, there are countless videos featuring devotional songs, bhajans, and stories about Krishna. Lastly, the popularity of podcasts has led to the emergence of shows that delve into the rich history and significance of Krishna, making the name even more accessible and relevant in today's world.

name_in_real_life.story: Lakshmi Krishnaa, a teacher in Hyderabad, India, shares that their name Krishnaa meaning "Darkness, Blackness" has been a constant source of inspiration, motivating them to follow Hindu values and serve their community.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Krishnaa symbolizes divine love and playfulness. As an embodiment of Vishnu, she represents the power to attract and preserve all things, engaging the world with her irresistible charm.
